tasks.reportMarkdown:
### Executive Summary
Across 15 threads spanning April–November 2026 in the **Claude experiment** Google Chat space (`spaces/AAQAly3tMR0`), Plentify teammates have moved well beyond basic chat into **Claude Code (CLI & VS Code)** workflows for weekday inbox triage, calendar-anchored planning, multi-repo onboarding, legacy tech-debt cleanup, and hardware/brand prototyping. Alongside clear productivity wins, the team flagged critical guardrails around **Fable 5.2's 30-day data retention and heavy token burn**, **complex PCB/UI rework**, **tone/brand-template drift**, and **strict production firmware boundaries**.

---

### 1. Standout Inbox, Calendar & Personal Productivity Setups
* **07:20 Draft-Only Inbox Assistant — Tumisang Kalagobe ("Ampere" / "Amp"):**
  * Runs every weekday at **07:20** to label inbox threads, flag quiet partner/deal threads, draft replies, and deliver a one-page priority brief—leaving Tumisang ~15 minutes to review and send (strictly draft-only, human-in-the-loop). He packaged this into a reusable Cowork starter-kit prompt.
  * Also built a Cowork **"Claude for academics"** OneDrive system (using a voice-profile doc and trackers) and an **MDU prospecting engine** in Claude Code that compresses 10–20 minutes/lead of manual research into batch prequalification, ICP scoring, and decision-maker matching.
* **"Plan My Day" & Cross-Tool PM Assistant — Taya Powers:**
  * Connected Claude Code to **Gmail, Google Calendar, Drive, Granola, Asana, Figma, Zoho Desk**, and a **read-only backend follower database** (saving ~4 hours on a single day).
  * Uses a `"plan my day"` prompt to structure **1 priority, 2–3 focus blocks, meeting buffers, and a concrete first step**, plus automated task capture, Madikwe resident app usage lookups, and a **12-month churn report** categorizing structural vs. optional cancellations.
* **Asana-Anchored Context — Graeme Longman:**
  * Uses Claude Code all day with **Asana, Google Drive, and Google Calendar** connectors; routes ad hoc tasks to a private Asana board and pastes Asana task links straight into sessions so Claude pulls full task and linked-doc context immediately.
* **Obsidian "Second Brain" — Kenau Struwig & Aadil Khoodoruth:**
  * **Kenau** runs scheduled Claude skills and MCPs to ingest notes and meeting transcripts into a backlinked Obsidian knowledge base and automate bulk admin.
  * **Aadil** logs multi-agent work in Obsidian so parallel sessions retain historical context.

---

### 2. Engineering, Hardware & Data Highlights
* **Claude Code & VS Code Dominance:** In **Steven Cooper**'s July 30 survey, **CLI / Claude Code** led decisively (13+ votes vs. 6 for Claude App UI). **Arno Scholtz**, **Caleb Smit**, **Aadil Khoodoruth**, and **Matthew Coulson** favor the **VS Code extension** over raw terminal CLI to avoid text-jumbling UI glitches. **Julian Banks** and **Aadil** both recommended **Herdr (`herdr.dev`)** for managing multiple agents and preserving CLI context if a terminal closes.
* **Interactive Repo Onboarding & Infra Automation — Keelan Govender & Jane Wyngaard:**
  * **Keelan** published org-scoped interactive repo onboarding guides (`ONBOARDING.md` → `claude.ai/claude-code/onboard/...`), wired **AWS S3 security reports** into infra repo remediation summaries, and used cross-repo discovery for **RDS/Redshift decommissioning**.
  * **Jane** uses Claude to navigate **~40–50 repos**, distilling research docs and converting repeatable tasks into deterministic scripts so she stops spending tokens re-running the same work.
* **Production Code Boundaries & Tech-Debt Wins:**
  * **Steven Cooper** refuses direct AI edits on production **Solarbot/Swattbot firmware** (limiting Claude to logging and review), while vibe-coding the **Solarbot Simulator** (EnergiTrack simulation) in ~2 hours.
  * **Eben Oladutemu** fixed a **User App** edit-routine reload state bug and accelerated **Ruby Solar Lane** work.
  * **Sheila Mbadi** used Fable (while included at a capped rate) to clear multi-year tech debt upgrading **WeasyPrint** (`pydyf` vs. `cairo` PDF rendering shifts) for HotBot user reports.
  * **Matthew Coulson** sped up **Inverter Digital Twin** EDA and outlier charting; **Arno Scholtz** built repeatable data queries/dashboards on `sims.plentify.io` (GORKs, Mantis, 2G sunset, meshing, refurb issues); and **Aadil** prototyped excess-solar and scheduled **EV charging** modes on the Solarbot repo.
* **Hardware & PCB Exploration — Irshaad Dodia & Craig Burden:**
  * **Irshaad** rated Claude **7/7** for navigating Plentify's hardware knowledge base—tracing wiring across boards, reading component datasheets, and suggesting alternatives—and noted simple HW designs succeeded with minimal intervention.
  * **Craig** used **Fable 5.2** in his spare time to prototype a complex **Raspberry Pi Compute Module 5 carrier board** (for monitor-mounted production/ops stations), showing strong exploratory value despite a messy first-prompt PCB that required extensive rework.

---

### 3. Brand, Visuals & Animations
* **"Make it Plentify" Brand Kit — Chris Vey & Tamsyn Lunt:** **Chris** packaged Marketing's Brand Refresh into a drop-in `Plentify-Brand-Kit.md` for Claude Projects to style internal `.docx` outputs. **Tamsyn** noted doc headers still didn't 100% match Marketing's Google Doc templates (and `.docx` → Google Doc conversion felt tedious), whereas feeding a **PDF of a preferred deck** worked far better; **Tumisang** suggested editing blank local templates via Cowork/Code for strict consistency.
* **Presentation Animations — Jon Kornik:** Tested **Opus 5.5** on presentation GIFs (`Shiftable-appliances-image-comp-2.gif` → `Load management with batteries.gif`), successfully adding batteries while preserving the original theme, colours, and background.
* **Upcoming Experiment — Emma Hobson:** Joined on November 16 to consolidate customer feedback on the **Balwin app**.

---

### 4. Key Risks, Model Notes & Friction Flagged by the Team
* **Fable 5.2 Data Retention & Token Drain:** **Keelan Govender** warned that Anthropic retains **Fable** data for **30 days** regardless of subscription tier (avoid sharing sensitive company data), and **Aadil Khoodoruth** cautioned that Fable 5.2 rapidly burned through most of his weekly tokens (noting the free weekly reset applies *only* to Fable).
* **Opus 5.5 vs. Sonnet & Claude Design:** **Aadil** praised **Opus 5.5** for deep data/log analysis with surprisingly low token usage, while **Sonnet** remains the everyday workhorse. Both **Marelieze Dreyer** and **Aadil** noted **Claude Design** burns tokens quickly and drifts from custom UI design systems unless outputs are iterated as images in Claude Chat.
* **Tone-of-Voice & UI Bugs:** **Tamsyn Lunt** flagged sycophancy and overly theatrical prose ("open mic night for slam poetry") plus a November 11 browser UI bug where Projects temporarily disappeared after an update (resolved via support/re-login; local files were intact).
* **Governance Discipline:** **Jon Kornik** enforces monthly value check-ins to retain seats, and **Tumisang** emphasized always treating AI as a draft-only assistant requiring thorough human review.

---

### Optional Next Steps (Available on Your Approval)
* **No external actions were staged or executed.** If you would like me to stage any follow-ups—such as a Google Doc digest of these workflows, a Knowledge Base brief (`KB-RES-07`) capturing team guardrails like Fable 5.2's 30-day retention warning, or a reply in the `Claude experiment` space—just let me know.

* **Weekday 07:20 Draft-Only Executive Assistant (Tumisang Kalagobe / "Ampere"):**

**Executive Summary:** Across Plentify's *Claude experiment* space (`spaces/AAQAly3tMR0`, Apr–Nov 2026), engineering, hardware, data, and brand teams have converged on **Claude Code (CLI and VS Code extension)** as a daily force multiplier for repo onboarding, legacy tech-debt cleanup, hardware knowledge navigation, and presentation/brand assets. At the same time, teammates flagged concrete guardrails around **Fable 5.2's 30-day data retention and rapid token burn**, **complex PCB/UI design rework**, **brand/tone-of-voice drift**, and **production firmware boundaries**.

---

### 1. Cross-Team Themes (`cross_team_themes`)

* **CLI & IDE Dominance Over Web UI:** In Steven Cooper's July 30 tooling survey, **CLI / Claude Code won overwhelmingly (13+ votes vs. 6 for Claude App UI)**. Multiple engineers (Arno Scholtz, Caleb Smit, Aadil Khoodoruth, Matthew Coulson) favor the **VS Code extension** over raw terminal CLI to avoid terminal text-jumbling/duplication and improve diff/file ergonomics.
* **Multi-Agent Orchestration & Persistent Context:** Power users are moving beyond single-session prompts. Julian Banks and Aadil Khoodoruth highlighted **Herdr (`herdr.dev`)** for multi-agent terminal multiplexing and preserving CLI context if a terminal closes, while Aadil integrates Claude with **Obsidian** to track parallel agent work over time.
* **Model Tiering & Token Economics:**
  * **Sonnet** serves as the daily workhorse.
  * **Opus 5 / Opus 5.5** is praised by Aadil Khoodoruth and Arno Scholtz for deep log/data analysis, bug hunting, and *low token burn* (Aadil noted he stopped hitting daily limits on Opus 5.5).
  * **Fable 5.2** (and **Claude Design**) drew caution for rapidly consuming weekly token quotas.
* **Repo Onboarding & Cost-Aware Automation:** Teams use Claude to bridge unfamiliar codebases (e.g., Ruby, hardware schematics, 40–50 repos), but experienced users like Jane Wyngaard actively script repeatable automations and maintain distilled research docs so they do not burn tokens re-deriving the same context.
* **Value Accountability:** Jon Kornik coordinates the space with regular "share your wisdom" value check-ins (e.g., onboarding Eben Oladutemu, Chris Vey, Dewald de Vos, Kailas Nair, and Emma Hobson) to justify and retain seats.

---

### 2. Standout Technical & Product Experiments (`standout_technical_and_product_experiments`)

* **Repo Onboarding, Security & Infra Decommissioning:**
  * **Keelan Govender** used Claude Code to publish org-scoped interactive onboarding guides (`ONBOARDING.md` → `claude.ai/claude-code/onboard/...`), wire **AWS S3 security reports** into infra repo remediation summaries, and run cross-repo discovery for **RDS/Redshift decommissioning**.
  * **Jane Wyngaard** navigates **~40–50 repos**, distilling findings into persistent research docs and deterministic scripts.
* **Software, Firmware & Simulation:**
  * **Steven Cooper** keeps production **Solarbot/Swattbot firmware** off-limits for direct Claude edits (restricting it to logging and review), while "vibe-coding" the **Solarbot Simulator** (EnergiTrack simulation) in ~2 hours.
  * **Eben Oladutemu** resolved a **User App** edit-routine reload bug (state lost from memory on page refresh) with minimal code changes and accelerated **Ruby Solar Lane** feature work and PR reviews.
  * **Sheila Mbadi** leveraged Fable (when capped/included) to clear multi-year tech debt upgrading **WeasyPrint** (`pydyf` vs. `cairo` PDF rendering shifts) for **HotBot** user reports.
  * **Matthew Coulson** accelerated **Inverter Digital Twin** exploratory data analysis (EDA) and outlier charting; **Arno Scholtz** built repeatable data queries and dashboards on `sims.plentify.io` covering production/procurement, GORKs, Mantis, 2G sunset, meshing, and refurb issues.
* **Hardware & PCB Exploration:**
  * **Irshaad Dodia** gave Claude access to Plentify's HW knowledge base to trace wiring across boards, read component datasheets, and suggest alternatives—rating it **7/7** for onboarding onto unfamiliar hardware designs and handling simple HW tasks.
  * **Craig Burden** used **Fable 5.2** in his spare time to prototype a complex **Raspberry Pi CM5 carrier board** (for monitor-mounted production/ops stations), demonstrating rapid feasibility exploration despite heavy rework needs.

  * **Deprecated:** `unread_gmail_count` (sourced from `INBOX` = `201`) and unfiltered `INBOX` `recent_emails`.

### Executive Summary
Across 15 threads (May–November 2026) in the **Claude experiment** Google Chat space (`spaces/AAQAly3tMR0`), Plentify staff have progressed from basic chat prompting to building automated inbox/PM assistants, read-only database analytics, multi-agent CLI workflows, and even experimental PCB hardware layouts. The highest-signal takeaways center on **Opus 5.5** and **MCP/Workspace connectors** driving major daily time savings—paired with clear guardrails around **Fable 5.2** token burn, 30-day data retention, and mandatory human-in-the-loop review.

---

### 1. Standout Executive, PM & Business Development Workflows
* **Tumisang Kalagobe — "Ampere" (Amp) Inbox Assistant & BD Engines:**
  * Built **Ampere**, an AI executive assistant that runs every weekday at `07:20` to label his inbox, draft replies, flag quiet threads, and produce a one-page summary of must-win deals—letting him hit inbox zero in ~15 minutes of morning review (`2026-09-17`, `2026-11-06`). He strictly enforces human review (*"Nothing goes out without me. Amp drafts, I decide and refine"*) and packaged a Cowork setup kit for teammates.
  * Earlier built a **Claude Code MDU prospecting/prequalification engine** for SA multi-dwelling units that scores leads against ICP, estimates door count/energy fit, and matches decision-makers—compressing 10–20 minutes of manual research per lead into minutes (`2026-07-22`). Also shared a OneDrive `_Masters Cowork` folder architecture with a personal voice profile (`2026-07-13`).
* **Taya Powers — Connected PM Assistant & Direct Data Queries (`2026-10-12`, `2026-10-27`):**
  * Connected Claude Code across **Gmail, Google Calendar, Drive, Granola, Asana, Figma, Zoho Desk**, plus **read-only access to the backend follower database**—saving ~4 hours in a single day.
  * Uses `"plan my day"` to pull calendar + to-do lists into one top priority with focus blocks and meeting buffers, queries user behavior directly (e.g., Madikwe residents' October app usage for scoping), and generated a **12-month churn report** separating structural cancellations (moving house, switching to gas) from optional ones.
* **Graeme Longman — Asana-Anchored Productivity (`2026-09-16`):**
  * Runs Claude Code all day with **Asana, Google Drive, and Google Calendar** connectors; drops ad-hoc tasks into a `"Productivity"` session to update his private Asana board and pastes Asana links into new sessions so Claude automatically pulls linked docs for context.
* **Kenau Struwig & Aadil Khoodoruth — Obsidian "Second Brain" (`2026-08-06`, `2026-11-10`):**
  * Kenau built scheduled Claude skills that continuously file notes, docs, and transcripts into an **Obsidian** vault with backlinks across concepts, projects, and people. Aadil similarly logs multi-agent work into Obsidian so Claude can recover historical context.

---

### 2. Engineering, Hardware & Tech-Debt Highlights
* **Hardware Design vs. Knowledge-Base Navigation (`2026-11-13` – `2026-11-14`):**
  * **Irshaad Dodia** tested Claude on hardware design: good on simple designs with minimal intervention, while complex layouts still need heavy rework (*"I guess we still have jobs (for now...)"*). Where it truly shines is navigating Plentify's HW knowledge base—tracing wiring across boards, reading component datasheets, suggesting alternatives, and onboarding onto unfamiliar designs (`"7/7 would Calude again"`).
  * **Craig Burden** used **Fable 5.2** in his spare time to attempt a fairly complex **Raspberry Pi Compute Module 5 (CM5)** monitor-mount carrier board (from an unprioritized PRD for ops/production use), sharing screenshots showing the first-prompt PCB layout was *"a bit of a mess"* and required extensive rework.
* **Keelan Govender — Repo Onboarding Links & AWS Security (`2026-06-12`, `2026-07-15`):**
  * Discovered Claude Code can generate and publish org-scoped `ONBOARDING.md` links (e.g., for the Blockpower HotBot status report) so any teammate opens a guided Claude Code session preloaded with repo context.
  * Used Claude Code for cross-repo RDS/Redshift decommissioning discovery and automated reviews of AWS S3 security reports against the infra repo.
* **Sheila Mbadi — Multi-Year PDF Tech Debt Cleared (`2026-08-20`):**

### 1. Root Cause Diagnosis (`root_cause_diagnosis`)

1. **Snapshot Serialization Truncation (Primary Cause):**
   - The context header explicitly reports `Google Chat Spaces (6):`, which indicates the upstream `GET https://chat.googleapis.com/v1/spaces` call returned **6** space objects in memory.

Because `spaces/AAQAly3tMR0` ("Claude experiment") sits at index 5 (the 6th item) in the API response order, it is silently truncated before reaching agents.
2. **Secondary Possibility — Per-Space Hydration Drop:**
   - Spaces 4 and 5 (`Notify me when I'm mentioned in spaces` and `Integration`) render with `(no recent messages)`, confirming that empty/quiet spaces are not filtered out by message count.

# Village Optimization Blueprint: Top 10 Cross-Department Improvements

**Prepared by:** Aria, Director of Research & Intel  
**Reviewed Inputs:** Zoe's Worker Draft, Cross-Department Courtyard Syncs (All Houses), Live Workspace Context (2026-11-13)  
**Governance Status:** Ready for CHO Review (Village Constitution Rules #1–#5 Verified)

---

## Executive Overview & Grounding Audit

Following your request for all houses to research improvements and compare notes, this report merges courtyard syncs from **Inbox & Calendar (Sam)**, **Operations House (Eli)**, **Finance & Money (Leo)**, **Health & Home (Owen)**, **Creative & Comms (Nora)**, **YouTube Studio (Maya)**, **Systems & Dev (Toby)**, and **Research & Intel (Aria & Zoe)** with live Gmail and Calendar telemetry.

**Source Grounding & Tool Gap Note:** Live Google Search tooling was unavailable during this final synthesis pass. To maintain strict intellectual honesty, no external statistics or URLs were fabricated; unverified newsletter claims cited in Zoe's draft (such as automated procurement settlement rates) remain flagged for live Google Search verification prior to any tooling commitment.

### Audit of Worker Draft (Zoe): Key Corrections & Elevations
- **Constitution Safeguards Added:** Zoe's proposals for autonomous AI procurement (#1) and IoT hardware sensors (#3) omitted mandatory CHO spend approval gates (Rule #2), while the internal skills marketplace (#4) needed explicit alignment with the Matt -> Town Hall -> CHO hiring workflow (Rule #4).
- **Calendar & Scope Alignment:** Zoe proposed introducing 90-day sprints (#5) and a complex digital twin (#8), overlooking that the village already runs `Sprint planning` (2026-11-16) and `Weekly Backend Check-in` (2026-11-17). We replaced buzzword-heavy simulation with practical Q4 budget variance and capacity modeling.
- **Single Source of Truth vs. Decentralization:** Corrected Zoe's decentralized wiki (#6) to a centralized knowledge repository to prevent SOP drift.
- **Cross-House Integration:** Incorporated critical sync notes missing from Zoe's draft—specifically Nora's messaging consistency, Maya's 30-second retention/B-roll pipeline, Eli's queue load balancing, Leo's Q4 variance checkpoints, and Sam's draft-staging queue.

---

## Top 10 Priorities to Make the Village Better

### 1. Daily Priority Triage & Draft-Staging Workflow
- **Leads:** Sam (Inbox & Calendar) + Eli (Operations House)
- **Problem:** Live Gmail shows **201 unread messages**, mixing critical updates (such as the `Morning Planning Brief - 2026-11-13`) with vendor newsletters (Twilio, Alibaba Cloud, Digital Twin Consortium).
- **Action:** Split morning inbox triage into two tracks—auto-digesting promotional noise while routing priority threads into clean response **drafts** queued for rapid CHO sign-off.
- **Guardrail:** All outbound replies strictly remain drafts until explicit CHO approval (Rule #1).

### 2. Calendar-Anchored Focus Blocks, Recovery & Crisis Buffers
- **Leads:** Owen (Health & Home) + Sam (Inbox & Calendar)
- **Problem:** Unexpected email bursts and operational interruptions threaten deep work and personal recovery.
- **Action:** Upgrade Zoe's wellness and 10% buffer concepts by locking dedicated deep-work windows, Owen's workout/recovery slots, and daily triage buffers directly around existing `Home` blocks (Nov 13, 16, 17) and pre-meeting windows.

### 3. Standardized Inter-House Handoff Checklists & Queue Balancing
- **Leads:** Eli (Operations House) + All Directors
- **Problem:** Work flows informally between Research, Comms, YouTube, and Finance, risking uneven worker loads across Leo, Zoe, Sam, Maya, Owen, and Toby.
- **Action:** Deploy a lightweight 5-point handoff checklist (scope, source validation, Constitution compliance, target owner, deadline) alongside weekly worker queue load balancing ahead of `Weekly Backend Check-in`.

### 4. Zero-Spend AI Model & Vendor Evaluation Sandbox
- **Leads:** Toby (Systems & Dev) + Leo (Finance & Money) + Aria (Research)
- **Problem:** Rapid model releases appearing in the inbox (e.g., Gemini 4 Carbon API, Qwen4 $3/mo plans) create vendor evaluation noise, while Zoe's autonomous negotiation concept introduces financial commitment risk.
- **Action:** Establish a structured, zero-spend technical and cost-comparison benchmark rubric. Any API trial, subscription, or procurement recommendation pauses at a comparative memo—never auto-purchasing or auto-contracting.
- **Guardrail:** Zero money spent or subscriptions purchased without explicit CHO approval (Rule #2).

### 5. Automated Pre-Flight Constitution Compliance Checks
- **Leads:** Toby (Systems & Dev) + Eli (Operations House)
- **Problem:** Manual enforcement of Village Rules #1–#5 across six active houses increases review burden on the CHO.
- **Action:** Build automated pre-submission checks verifying that every deliverable returned to the CHO contains zero auto-sent emails, zero unapproved spend commitments, zero public posts, and clean PDF-ready Markdown formatting (Rules #1, #2, #3, #5).

### 6. Centralized Village Knowledge Base (Single Source of Truth)
- **Leads:** Aria & Zoe (Research & Intel) + Eli (Operations House)
- **Problem:** Zoe's decentralized wiki suggestion risks contradictory SOPs and duplicated courtyard syncs.
- **Action:** Consolidate the Village Constitution, house memory notes, handoff templates, and verified research briefs into one indexed internal knowledge repository so every worker operates from identical ground truth.

### 7. Sprint-Synced Q4 Budget Variance & Capacity Forecasting
- **Leads:** Leo (Finance & Money) + Eli (Operations House)
- **Problem:** Building a full physical/digital twin (Zoe #8) is over-engineered for current needs, whereas Q4 budget drift and sprint bottlenecks require immediate visibility.
- **Action:** Embed Leo's Q4 budget variance checkpoints and simple capacity/what-if scenarios directly into the existing `Sprint planning` (Mondays) and `Company meeting` (Tuesdays) cadence.

### 8. Unified Research-to-Comms-to-YouTube Creative Pipeline
- **Leads:** Nora (Creative & Comms) + Maya (YouTube Studio) + Aria (Research)
- **Problem:** External omnichannel consistency suffers if campaign messaging and video production operate in silos.
- **Action:** Connect Research briefs directly to Nora's campaign messaging templates and Maya's YouTube production checklists—standardizing opening 30-second retention hooks and B-roll cues before any asset reaches review.
- **Guardrail:** Zero content published to YouTube, social media, or newsletters without explicit CHO approval (Rule #3).

### 9. Audio-First Executive Read-Aheads for Packed Calendar Days
- **Leads:** Sam (Inbox & Calendar) + Nora (Creative & Comms)
- **Problem:** Dense written reports create review friction on heavy meeting days (`Sprint planning`, `Weekly Backend Check-in`, `Company meeting`).
- **Action:** Mirror the `Morning Planning Brief` spoken-summary workflow by pairing crisp written executive deliverables (Rule #5) with optional 60-second audio-ready executive scripts for rapid asynchronous review.

### 10. Internal Skills Matrix & Governed Hiring Escalation Protocol
- **Leads:** Eli (Operations House) + Matt (Talent Sourcing)
- **Problem:** Minor cross-house workload spikes can delay execution if capabilities across existing workers are opaque.
- **Action:** Maintain an internal skills and availability matrix to reallocate existing worker capacity first; whenever a true capability gap persists, trigger the mandatory Village Constitution pipeline—Matt sources the candidate, the CHO interviews in Town Hall, and the CHO grants explicit approval (Rule #4).

---

## Immediate Implementation Roadmap (Nov 13 – Nov 17)
- **Today (2026-11-13):** Sam triages the 201-email backlog and stages high-priority drafts; Owen and Sam align focus/recovery buffers around `Home` blocks.
- **Monday (2026-11-16, 09:00):** Present Top 10 priorities selected by the CHO at `Sprint planning` to lock Q4 deliverables, handoff checklists, and Leo's budget checkpoints.
- **Tuesday (2026-11-17, 10:00 & 16:00):** Review Toby's pre-flight compliance checks during `Weekly Backend Check-in` and formalize the cross-house operating cadence at the `Company meeting`.

kbProposals.title: Autonomous Town Triggers & Supervised Execution Rules
kbProposals.summary: Defines the 3-layer Supervised Autonomy architecture, scheduled SAST heartbeats, Workspace webhook rules, fail-closed headless guardrails, and KB-GOV-01 approval boundaries for autonomous town execution.
kbProposals.details:
### 1. Purpose & Governance Boundary
This brief establishes the canonical rules for running Guildhaven proactively in **Supervised Autonomy** mode. Agents may execute internal read, research, triage, and drafting workflows without a CHO prompt, but **must** strictly enforce `KB-GOV-01` (Village Constitution): all external writes, spend, public posts, and live KB mutations pause in **Pending CHO Approvals**.

---

### 2. Three-Layer Supervised Autonomy Architecture

#### Layer 1: Wake-Up Engine (Triggers)
1. **Scheduled Heartbeats (Cron — `Africa/Johannesburg` / SAST):**
   - **07:30 SAST (Weekdays) — Morning Triage:** Scan today's Calendar, monitored Gmail labels (`KB-SOP-06`), and Plentify OOO; stage Morning Prep or Focus Buffers if needed.
   - **12:30 SAST (Weekdays) — Midday Replan:** Check watched Google Chat spaces (*Product Operations*, *Backend*, *Integration*, *Tiger T: Balwin*) for unresolved `@mentions` or blockers; stage thread replies with `chatThreadName` pre-filled.
   - **Monday 08:00 SAST — Weekly KB & Sprint Hygiene:** Audit recurring cross-house friction and stage `propose_kb_entry` proposals if needed.
2. **Event-Driven Webhooks (`KB-RES-02`):**
   - Trigger on monitored Gmail labels (e.g., Gemini Meeting Notes, Bitbucket PR tags, priority threads) or watched Google Chat space events.
   - Verify HMAC signature or Google OIDC push token on the raw request body, reject timestamps >5 minutes old, and dedupe via deterministic `idempotency_key`.
   - Always hydrate the full thread before acting—never draft from truncated snippets.

#### Layer 2: Safe-Zone Headless Runner (`KB-SOP-01`)
- Executes `Matt` triage → `Guild Specialist` draft → `Director` verification silently in the background.
- **Strict Tool Whitelist:** Background runs may **only** invoke read-only Workspace/Search/KB tools, `dispatch_handoff`, `stage_cho_decision_packet`, and `propose_kb_entry`. Direct external writes are blocked at runtime.
- **Fail-Closed Caps:** Abort with `failed_closed` if execution exceeds `max_job_duration_ms` (30s) or `max_agent_hops` (4), logging the partial trace without staging incomplete packets.
- **Global Kill-Switch:** Honor `town_settings.autopilot_enabled`; when `false`, all cron and webhook runs halt immediately.

#### Layer 3: Decoupled HITL Queue & Quiet Digest
- **Pending CHO Approvals:** Actionable deliverables are staged as `cho_decision_packets` tagged with `source_trigger` (`cron` | `webhook` | `chat`) and a `ttl_expires_at` (default 24h) so stale drafts auto-expire.
- **Town Digest:** Non-actionable runs log a concise 1–2 sentence summary in `automation_runs` without interrupting the CHO.

I’ve synthesized our internal village audit (`KB-GOV-02`, `KB-RES-01`, `KB-RES-03`, and Zoe’s worker draft) with external research on multi-agent systems and Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) workflow UX.

Across the Village, most friction doesn't come from lack of capability—it comes from **context loss between handoffs**, **unscoped inbox noise**, and **approval friction** where you have to hunt for context before signing off.

Here are the highest-leverage improvements to make the Village and app faster, calmer, and easier to run:

---

### 1. Turn CHO Approvals into 10–30 Second "Decision Packets" (App UX)
Under `KB-GOV-01`, emails, calendar writes, spend, and public posts rightly stay gated behind your approval. However, bare "Approve?" prompts create review fatigue and slow you down.
* **Add Evidence Packs & Edit-in-Place:** Every approval card should display the exact diff/draft, the `KB-*` or source links behind it, and reversibility/cost—allowing you to tweak one line and approve in 10–30 seconds rather than rewriting.
* **Batch Low-Risk Drafts & Surface Exceptions First:** Group routine Gmail drafts into a single batched review queue, and pin failed, blocked, or low-confidence items to the top so exceptions get attention first.
* **Keep Safe Work Frictionless:** Keep read-only research and internal draft staging automated within strict limits, reserving pause gates strictly for irreversible or external side effects (`KB-GOV-01`).

---

### 2. Clear the 201-Email Backlog with Scoped Triage & Focus Buffers (Operations & Inbox)
* **Strict Label Scoping:** Lock automated Gmail scanning to our 4 designated team labels (starting with *Planning Briefs*, as scoped with Daniel and Devon) so irrelevant mail stops crowding triage.
* **Structured Backlog & Focus Windows:** Pair `KB-SOP-05` draft-only follow-up batching with protected calendar focus buffers (`KB-RES-03`) so backlog clearing happens in predictable blocks instead of continuous interruptions.

---

### 3. Replace Conversational Handoffs with Strict "Contract Packets" (Cross-House Architecture)
Multi-agent workflows most often break when context is passed implicitly through chat history rather than structured state.
* **Enforce Typed Handoff Fields:** Every transfer across `KB-SOP-01`–`04` should pass a compact contract—**verified facts, source dates/`KB-*` IDs, hard constraints, and target output schema**—rather than long prose summaries.
* **Keep Hub-and-Spoke Routing:** Route tasks cleanly (`Matt` → `Director` → `Specialist` → `Director`) instead of ad-hoc specialist-to-specialist hops, which show the highest context loss and rework.
* **Retire Redundant Courtyard Syncs:** Have workers read and log state directly to the Centralized Knowledge Base (`KB-GOV-02`, `KB-RES-01`) to eliminate repetitive status checks.

---

### 4. Harden Reliability & Cost Guardrails (Systems & Finance)
* **Fail Closed + Loop Caps:** Ensure stalled tasks, missing approvals, or loop/token budgets fail closed cleanly and alert Operations rather than spinning silently (`KB-RES-02`).
* **Pre-Gated Spend Packets:** Keep `KB-SOP-04`’s 3-option vendor matrix mandatory before any subscription or purchase reaches your approval queue so financial decisions take one look.

---

### Ready for Your Direction

```ts
  id: string;                     // e.g., "cron_morning_triage", "webhook_gmail_monitored"
  name: string;
  type: "cron" | "webhook";
  enabled: boolean;
  schedule_cron?: string;         // e.g., "30 5 * * 1-5" (07:30 SAST = 05:30 UTC)
  timezone: string;               // Default: "Africa/Johannesburg"
  target_house: string;           // e.g., "daniel", "devon", "aria"
  config: {
    monitored_gmail_labels?: string[];  // Per KB-SOP-06 (e.g., ["INBOX_PRIORITY", "Meeting Notes"])
    ignore_unread_bulk?: boolean;       // e.g., ignore bulk unread inbox noise
    watched_chat_spaces?: string[];     // e.g., ["spaces/AAAAfTDLRF8", "spaces/AAAAaTh2I_Q"]
    packet_ttl_hours: number;           // Default: 24 (auto-expire stale packets)
  };
  last_run_at?: string;           // ISO-8601
  updated_at: string;
}
```

### B. `town_settings` (Global Kill-Switch)
```ts
interface TownAutopilotSettings {
  autopilot_enabled: boolean;     // Global Pause / Resume toggle
  max_runs_per_hour: number;      // Rate-limit guardrail (default: 20)
  max_job_duration_ms: number;    // Fail-closed timeout (default: 30000)
  max_agent_hops: number;         // Max handoffs per background run (default: 4)
}
```

### C. `automation_runs` (Audit & Quiet Digest Log)
```ts
interface AutomationRun {
  id: string;
  rule_id: string;
  idempotency_key: string;        // Unique constraint to prevent duplicate runs
  status: "completed" | "staged_packet" | "skipped_paused" | "failed_closed";
  summary: string;                // 1-2 sentence digest for the CHO feed
  staged_packet_ids: string[];    // Links to Pending CHO Approvals
  agent_trace: string[];          // e.g., ["matt", "worker_daniel", "daniel"]
  duration_ms: number;
  created_at: string;
}
```

### D. `cho_decision_packets` Extensions
Add the following fields to existing Decision Packets:
- `source_trigger`: `"chat" | "cron" | "webhook"`
- `automation_run_id?: string`
- `ttl_expires_at?: string` (ISO-8601; expired packets auto-transition to `expired` status)

---

## 4. Backend API Routes

### 1. `POST /api/cron/heartbeat`
- **Auth:** Require `Authorization: Bearer <CRON_SECRET>` header (fail-closed `401` if missing/invalid).
- **Behavior:**
  1. Check `town_settings.autopilot_enabled`. If `false`, return `200 { status: "paused" }`.
  2. Query `town_automation_rules` where `type = "cron"` and `enabled = true` due for the current window.
  3. Generate deterministic `idempotency_key` (`${rule.id}:${date_hour_bucket}`). Skip if already in `automation_runs`.
  4. Execute the headless `KB-SOP-01` runner with `max_job_duration_ms` and `max_agent_hops`.
  5. Record result in `automation_runs` (and `cho_decision_packets` if a deliverable was staged).

### 2. `POST /api/webhooks/workspace`
- **Auth & Verification (`KB-RES-02`):**
  - Verify HMAC signature or Google OIDC push token on the **raw request body** before JSON parsing.
  - Reject timestamps older than 5 minutes (replay protection).
- **Behavior:**
  1. Check `autopilot_enabled` and matching `webhook` rule.
  2. Compute `idempotency_key` from the provider event ID / message ID. Return `200 { status: "duplicate_ignored" }` if already processed.
  3. Hydrate minimal context (e.g., fetch specific Gmail thread or Google Chat thread via `read_google_chat`—never act on truncated snippets alone).
  4. Run headless `KB-SOP-01` pipeline and stage a `cho_decision_packet` if action is needed.

### 3. `GET /api/automation/rules` & `PATCH /api/automation/rules`
- Allows the CHO to toggle `autopilot_enabled`, enable/disable individual rules, and configure `monitored_gmail_labels`, `watched_chat_spaces`, and `packet_ttl_hours`.

### 4. `GET /api/automation/runs`
- Returns recent `automation_runs` for the Town Digest feed, plus a background sweeper (or query-time check) that marks packets past `ttl_expires_at` as `expired`.

---

## 5. Headless Runner Guardrails (Fail-Closed)
1. **Strict Tool Whitelist:** In background mode (`mode = "autonomous"`), strip or block any tool that directly mutates external state. Only allow:
   - Read-only Workspace/Search/KB tools (`read_google_chat`, Gmail/Calendar/Drive readers, `google:search`)
   - `dispatch_handoff`
   - `stage_cho_decision_packet`
   - `propose_kb_entry`
2. **Token & OAuth Discipline (`KB-RES-02`):** Never persist raw OAuth access tokens in `automation_runs` or logs; use server-side refresh/service credentials or scoped session tokens.
3. **Budget & Loop Caps:** Abort with `failed_closed` if execution exceeds `max_job_duration_ms` (30s) or `max_agent_hops` (4), logging the partial trace to `automation_runs` without staging half-baked packets.

---

## 6. Default Automation Rules to Seed
1. **`cron_morning_triage` (`07:30 SAST`, Weekdays):** Scans today's Calendar, monitored Gmail labels (`KB-SOP-06`), and Plentify OOO; stages a Morning Prep / Focus Buffer packet if gaps or urgent items exist.
2. **`cron_midday_replan` (`12:30 SAST`, Weekdays):** Checks watched Google Chat spaces (*Product Operations*, *Backend*, *Integration*, *Tiger T: Balwin*) for unresolved `@mentions` or blockers; stages thread replies (`chatThreadName` pre-filled).
3. **`cron_weekly_kb_hygiene` (`Monday 08:00 SAST`):** Audits recurring cross-house friction and stages `propose_kb_entry` updates if needed.
4. **`webhook_gmail_priority` (Event-Driven):** Triggers on new threads in CHO-monitored labels (e.g., Gemini meeting notes, Bitbucket PR tags, CS Insights); hydrates full thread and stages a Gmail draft.

---

## 7. Frontend UI Additions
1. **Autopilot Control Panel (Settings / Town Header):**
   - Prominent **Autopilot Pause / Resume** toggle.
   - Rule list with toggles, schedule/label config, and "Run Now" manual test button.
2. **Town Digest Feed:**
   - Lightweight activity stream showing background `automation_runs` (e.g., *"07:30 Morning Triage completed — no urgent actions needed"* or *"Staged 1 Gmail draft from Meeting Notes"*).
3. **Pending CHO Approvals Upgrades:**
   - Source badge on each packet (`Cron · 07:30 SAST`, `Webhook · Gmail`, or `Chat`).
   - TTL countdown badge (e.g., `Expires in 18h`) and a **Dismiss Expired / Clear All** control.

---

## 8. Acceptance Criteria (Test Checklist)
- [ ] **Kill-Switch:** Toggling `autopilot_enabled = false` immediately halts `/api/cron/heartbeat` and `/api/webhooks/workspace` without errors.
- [ ] **Idempotency:** Sending the same webhook payload or cron bucket twice executes only once.
- [ ] **Governance Boundary (`KB-GOV-01`):** A background run **cannot** send an email, create a calendar event, post to Google Chat, or edit the live KB—it only stages a `cho_decision_packet`.
- [ ] **Fail-Closed Timeout:** A simulated slow/hanging agent run aborts cleanly at `max_job_duration_ms` and logs `failed_closed` with no orphaned packets.
- [ ] **TTL Expiry:** Packets older than `ttl_expires_at` automatically leave the active Pending Approvals queue.

we need to generate a CRON_SECRET and WORKSPACE_WEBHOOK_SECRET

Because an AI chat model isn’t a cryptographic random number generator—and secrets shouldn’t be generated inside chat history—you should generate both secrets locally in your terminal or server environment using a proper CSPRNG.

Here is everything you need to generate, store, and wire up **`CRON_SECRET`** and **`WORKSPACE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`** per **`KB-RES-02`** and **`KB-RES-06`**:

---

### 1. Generate Cryptographically Strong Secrets (256-bit)

Run **one** of these in your terminal twice (once for each variable):

**macOS / Linux (`openssl`):**
```bash
openssl rand -hex 32
```

**Node.js (cross-platform):**
```bash
node -e "console.log(require('crypto').randomBytes(32).toString('hex'))"
```

**Python 3:**
```bash
python3 -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_hex(32))"
```

---

### 2. Store Them in Environment Variables (Never in Git)

Add the two generated 64-character hex strings to your local `.env.local` (for testing) and your production hosting environment (e.g., Vercel / Cloud Run / Railway):

```env
CRON_SECRET="your_first_64_char_hex_string"
WORKSPACE_WEBHOOK_SECRET="your_second_64_char_hex_string"
```

*(Make sure they are **two different** secrets so rotating one never affects the other.)*

---

### 3. How They Map to Your Endpoints (`KB-RES-06` & `KB-RES-02`)

1. **`CRON_SECRET` → `POST /api/cron/heartbeat`**
   - Your scheduler (Vercel Cron, Cloud Scheduler, GitHub Actions, etc.) sends:
     `Authorization: Bearer <CRON_SECRET>`
   - Your route handler validates it with a **constant-time comparison** (`crypto.timingSafeEqual`) and fails closed with `401` if missing or mismatched.

2. **`WORKSPACE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` → `POST /api/webhooks/workspace`**
   - Used to compute and verify the **HMAC-SHA256** signature against the **raw request body** (before `JSON.parse`) alongside a 5-minute timestamp replay check (`KB-RES-02`).
   - *Note:* If you wire Google Cloud Pub/Sub push directly without an HMAC relay, you can alternatively verify the Google-signed OIDC JWT on the push request, or pass a webhook secret token/header depending on your ingress setup.

---

knowledgeBase.title: Village Constitution & Human-in-the-Loop Governance
knowledgeBase.summary: Immutable executive guardrails governing Gmail drafts, spending, public publishing, production systems, and hiring.
knowledgeBase.contentMarkdown:
### Binding Governance Clauses
1. **Draft-Only Email Policy**: Every outbound email prepared by Inbox & Calendar or any guild house remains an un-sent draft until explicitly approved by the Chief Human Officer (CHO).
2. **Zero Autonomous Spend**: No Director or Guild Specialist may purchase SaaS subscriptions, authorize vendor invoices, or book paid travel without explicit CHO sign-off.
3. **Zero Unapproved Public Publishing**: Video uploads, social posts, and newsletters stay staged for CHO approval before external release.
4. **Production & Credentials Boundary**: Systems & Dev never rotates live production secrets or deploys breaking schema migrations without CHO authorization.
5. **Town Hall Hiring Protocol**: Every new Guild Specialist candidate is sourced by Matt, interviewed in Town Hall, and approved by the CHO.

knowledgeBase.title: Single Source of Truth Charter (Replacing Decentralized Wikis)
knowledgeBase.summary: Consolidates all SOPs, handoff contracts, house notes, and verified research into one indexed repository with Propose & Approve CHO governance.
knowledgeBase.contentMarkdown:
### Why Decentralized House Wikis Are Retired
- Separate per-house notes and informal wiki pages caused contradictory SOP steps and repeated courtyard status checks.
- **Canonical Ground Truth**: Every Director and Guild Specialist operates from this indexed `KB-*` repository.

### Propose & Approve Stewardship Protocol
- **Research & Intel (`Aria` & `Zoe`)** verify external facts, citations, and benchmark briefs (`KB-RES-*`).
- **Operations House (`Eli` & `Devon`)** maintain cross-house handoff templates and standard operating procedures (`KB-SOP-*`).
- **Zero Direct Agent Writes**: Agents propose updates via `propose_kb_entry` as `pending` CHO Decision Packets; only explicit CHO approval commits live `KB-*` versions.

knowledgeBase.title: Matt → Director → Guild Specialist Dispatch & Review SOP
knowledgeBase.summary: Standard 4-stage execution pipeline ensuring fast specialist drafting followed by executive Director verification.
knowledgeBase.contentMarkdown:
### Standard Execution Pipeline
1. **Triage (`Matt`)**: Classify incoming CHO request by primary house, determine whether live Google Search grounding is needed, and flag Advisor escalation or CHO approval gates.
2. **Specialist Draft (`Guild Specialist`)**: Execute initial research, code schema, or checklist against `KB-*` templates and live Google Workspace context.
3. **Director Audit (`House Director`)**: Verify accuracy, remove contradictions, enforce `KB-GOV-01`, and format executive Markdown for PDF export.
4. **Knowledge Indexing (`Aria, Zoe & Eli`)**: Reusable findings or recurring workflows are promoted into `KB-RES-*` or `KB-SOP-*` entries.

- **Auth & Scope Boundary**: Least-privilege OAuth2 scopes or server-side secret references (never client-exposed keys).
- **Idempotency & Retry Contract**: Deterministic `Idempotency-Key` header, exponential backoff with jitter, and dead-letter queue recovery.
- **Schema Mapping Table**: Canonical field types, nullability handling, and UTC ISO-8601 timestamps.
- **Rollout Checklist**: Dry-run payload verification by Toby, architecture sign-off by Kieran, and CHO approval before production cutover.

### Verified Findings
- **Root Cause Identified**: Maintaining separate per-guild mini-wikis caused drift between Operations checklists, Systems & Dev webhook specs, and Creative launch templates.
- **Resolution**: Indexing every governance clause (`KB-GOV-*`), handoff SOP (`KB-SOP-*`), verified brief (`KB-RES-*`), and consolidated house memory (`KB-MEM-*`) gives all 18 village members identical context.
- **Operational Impact**: Courtyard conversations now exchange delta updates tied to canonical `KB-*` IDs instead of re-deriving workflows from scratch.

knowledgeBase.title: API Reliability, OAuth Token Hygiene & Idempotent Event Pipelines
knowledgeBase.summary: Verified engineering reference for Google Workspace OAuth2 token handling, webhook signature verification, and resilient retries.
knowledgeBase.contentMarkdown:
### Canonical Engineering Standards
- **OAuth2 Memory Discipline**: Google Workspace access tokens live strictly in client memory and renew silently via Google Identity Services; only non-secret briefing metadata is snapshotted.
- **Webhook Verification**: Verify HMAC signatures on raw request bodies before JSON parsing and enforce 5-minute replay windows.
- **Idempotent Writes**: Deduplicate upstream retries on `(provider, event_id)` before mutating downstream state or queueing notifications.

knowledgeBase.title: Autonomous Town Triggers & Supervised Execution Rules
knowledgeBase.summary: Defines the 3-layer Supervised Autonomy architecture, scheduled SAST heartbeats, Workspace webhook rules, fail-closed headless guardrails, and KB-GOV-01 approval boundaries for autonomous town execution.
knowledgeBase.contentMarkdown:
### 1. Purpose & Governance Boundary
This brief establishes the canonical rules for running Guildhaven proactively in **Supervised Autonomy** mode. Agents may execute internal read, research, triage, and drafting workflows without a CHO prompt, but **must** strictly enforce `KB-GOV-01` (Village Constitution): all external writes, spend, public posts, and live KB mutations pause in **Pending CHO Approvals**.

---

### 2. Three-Layer Supervised Autonomy Architecture

#### Layer 1: Wake-Up Engine (Triggers)
1. **Scheduled Heartbeats (Cron — `Africa/Johannesburg` / SAST):**
   - **07:30 SAST (Weekdays) — Morning Triage:** Scan today's Calendar, monitored Gmail labels (`KB-SOP-06`), and Plentify OOO; stage Morning Prep or Focus Buffers if needed.
   - **12:30 SAST (Weekdays) — Midday Replan:** Check watched Google Chat spaces (*Product Operations*, *Backend*, *Integration*, *Tiger T: Balwin*) for unresolved `@mentions` or blockers; stage thread replies with `chatThreadName` pre-filled.
   - **Monday 08:00 SAST — Weekly KB & Sprint Hygiene:** Audit recurring cross-house friction and stage `propose_kb_entry` proposals if needed.
2. **Event-Driven Webhooks (`KB-RES-02`):**
   - Trigger on monitored Gmail labels (e.g., Gemini Meeting Notes, Bitbucket PR tags, priority threads) or watched Google Chat space events.
   - Verify HMAC signature or Google OIDC push token on the raw request body, reject timestamps >5 minutes old, and dedupe via deterministic `idempotency_key`.
   - Always hydrate the full thread before acting—never draft from truncated snippets.

#### Layer 2: Safe-Zone Headless Runner (`KB-SOP-01`)
- Executes `Matt` triage → `Guild Specialist` draft → `Director` verification silently in the background.
- **Strict Tool Whitelist:** Background runs may **only** invoke read-only Workspace/Search/KB tools, `dispatch_handoff`, `stage_cho_decision_packet`, and `propose_kb_entry`. Direct external writes are blocked at runtime.
- **Fail-Closed Caps:** Abort with `failed_closed` if execution exceeds `max_job_duration_ms` (30s) or `max_agent_hops` (4), logging the partial trace without staging incomplete packets.
- **Global Kill-Switch:** Honor `town_settings.autopilot_enabled`; when `false`, all cron and webhook runs halt immediately.

#### Layer 3: Decoupled HITL Queue & Quiet Digest
- **Pending CHO Approvals:** Actionable deliverables are staged as `cho_decision_packets` tagged with `source_trigger` (`cron` | `webhook` | `chat`) and a `ttl_expires_at` (default 24h) so stale drafts auto-expire.
- **Town Digest:** Non-actionable runs log a concise 1–2 sentence summary in `automation_runs` without interrupting the CHO.

linkedDocs.content:
Across 15 threads spanning April–November 2026 in the Claude experiment Google Chat space (spaces/AAQAly3tMR0), Plentify teammates have moved well beyond basic chat into Claude Code (CLI & VS Code) workflows for wee...

Prepared by Daniel (Guildhaven)

Executive Summary

Across 15 threads spanning April–November 2026 in the Claude experiment Google Chat space (spaces/AAQAly3tMR0), Plentify teammates have moved well beyond basic chat into Claude Code (CLI & VS Code) workflows for weekday inbox triage, calendar-anchored planning, multi-repo onboarding, legacy tech-debt cleanup, and hardware/brand prototyping. Alongside clear productivity wins, the team flagged critical guardrails around Fable 5.2's 30-day data retention and heavy token burn, complex PCB/UI rework, tone/brand-template drift, and strict production firmware boundaries.

---

1. Standout Inbox, Calendar & Personal Productivity Setups

 07:20 Draft-Only Inbox Assistant — Tumisang Kalagobe ("Ampere" / "Amp"):
   Runs every weekday at 07:20 to label inbox threads, flag quiet partner/deal threads, draft replies, and deliver a one-page priority brief—leaving Tumisang ~15 minutes to review and send (strictly draft-only, human-in-the-loop). He packaged this into a reusable Cowork starter-kit prompt.
   Also built a Cowork "Claude for academics" OneDrive system (using a voice-profile doc and trackers) and an MDU prospecting engine in Claude Code that compresses 10–20 minutes/lead of manual research into batch prequalification, ICP scoring, and decision-maker matching.
 "Plan My Day" & Cross-Tool PM Assistant — Taya Powers:
   Connected Claude Code to Gmail, Google Calendar, Drive, Granola, Asana, Figma, Zoho Desk, and a read-only backend follower database (saving ~4 hours on a single day).
   Uses a "plan my day" prompt to structure 1 priority, 2–3 focus blocks, meeting buffers, and a concrete first step, plus automated task capture, Madikwe resident app usage lookups, and a 12-month churn report categorizing structural vs. optional cancellations.
 Asana-Anchored Context — Graeme Longman:
   Uses Claude Code all day with Asana, Google Drive, and Google Calendar connectors; routes ad hoc tasks to a private Asana board and pastes Asana task links straight into sessions so Claude pulls full task and linked-doc context immediately.
 Obsidian "Second Brain" — Kenau Struwig & Aadil Khoodoruth:
   Kenau runs scheduled Claude skills and MCPs to ingest notes and meeting transcripts into a backlinked Obsidian knowledge base and automate bulk admin.
   Aadil logs multi-agent work in Obsidian so parallel sessions retain historical context.

---

2. Engineering, Hardware & Data Highlights

 Claude Code & VS Code Dominance: In Steven Cooper's July 30 survey, CLI / Claude Code led decisively (13+ votes vs. 6 for Claude App UI). Arno Scholtz, Caleb Smit, Aadil Khoodoruth, and Matthew Coulson favor the VS Code extension over raw terminal CLI to avoid text-jumbling UI glitches. Julian Banks and Aadil both recommended Herdr (herdr.dev) for managing multiple agents and preserving CLI context if a terminal closes.
 Interactive Repo Onboarding & Infra Automation — Keelan Govender & Jane Wyngaard:
   Keelan published org-scoped interactive repo onboarding guides (ONBOARDING.md → claude.ai/claude-code/onboard/...), wired AWS S3 security reports into infra repo remediation summaries, and used cross-repo discovery for RDS/Redshift decommissioning.
   Jane uses Claude to navigate ~40–50 repos, distilling research docs and converting repeatable tasks into deterministic scripts so she stops spending tokens re-running the same work.
 Production Code Boundaries & Tech-Debt Wins:
   Steven Cooper refuses direct AI edits on production Solarbot/Swattbot firmware (limiting Claude to logging and review), while vibe-coding the Solarbot Simulator (EnergiTrack simulation) in ~2 hours.
   Eben Oladutemu fixed a User App edit-routine reload state bug and accelerated Ruby Solar Lane work.
   Sheila Mbadi used Fable (while included at a capped rate) to clear multi-year tech debt upgrading WeasyPrint (pydyf vs. cairo PDF rendering shifts) for HotBot user reports.
   Matthew Coulson sped up Inverter Digital Twin EDA and outlier charting; Arno Scholtz built repeatable data queries/dashboards on sims.plentify.io (GORKs, Mantis, 2G sunset, meshing, refurb issues); and Aadil prototyped excess-solar and scheduled EV charging modes on the Solarbot repo.
 Hardware & PCB Exploration — Irshaad Dodia & Craig Burden:
   Irshaad rated Claude 7/7 for navigating Plentify's hardware knowledge base—tracing wiring across boards, reading component datasheets, and suggesting alternatives—and noted simple HW designs succeeded with minimal intervention.
   Craig used Fable 5.2 in his spare time to prototype a complex Raspberry Pi Compute Module 5 carrier board (for monitor-mounted production/ops stations), showing strong exploratory value despite a messy first-prompt PCB that required extensive rework.

---

3. Brand, Visuals & Animations

 "Make it Plentify" Brand Kit — Chris Vey & Tamsyn Lunt: Chris packaged Marketing's Brand Refresh into a drop-in Plentify-Brand-Kit.md for Claude Projects to style internal .docx outputs. Tamsyn noted doc headers still didn't 100% match Marketing's Google Doc templates (and .docx → Google Doc conversion felt tedious), whereas feeding a PDF of a preferred deck worked far better; Tumisang suggested editing blank local templates via Cowork/Code for strict consistency.
 Presentation Animations — Jon Kornik: Tested Opus 5.5 on presentation GIFs (Shiftable-appliances-image-comp-2.gif → Load management with batteries.gif), successfully adding batteries while preserving the original theme, colours, and background.
 Upcoming Experiment — Emma Hobson: Joined on November 16 to consolidate customer feedback on the Balwin app.

---

4. Key Risks, Model Notes & Friction Flagged by the Team

 Fable 5.2 Data Retention & Token Drain: Keelan Govender warned that Anthropic retains Fable data for 30 days regardless of subscription tier (avoid sharing sensitive company data), and Aadil Khoodoruth cautioned that Fable 5.2 rapidly burned through most of his weekly tokens (noting the free weekly reset applies only to Fable).
 Opus 5.5 vs. Sonnet & Claude Design: Aadil praised Opus 5.5 for deep data/log analysis with surprisingly low token usage, while Sonnet remains the everyday workhorse. # give me a summary of interesting things in the Claude experiment (https://chat.google.com/room/AAQAly3tMR0?cls=0) chat space

**Executive Summary:** Across 15 threads spanning April–November 2026 in the Claude experiment Google Chat space (`spaces/AAQAly3tMR0`), Plentify teammates have moved well beyond basic chat into Claude Code (CLI & VS Code) workflows for wee...

*Prepared by Daniel · Guildhaven*

---

### Executive Summary
Across 15 threads spanning April–November 2026 in the **Claude experiment** Google Chat space (`spaces/AAQAly3tMR0`), Plentify teammates have moved well beyond basic chat into **Claude Code (CLI & VS Code)** workflows for weekday inbox triage, calendar-anchored planning, multi-repo onboarding, legacy tech-debt cleanup, and hardware/brand prototyping. Alongside clear productivity wins, the team flagged critical guardrails around **Fable 5.2's 30-day data retention and heavy token burn**, **complex PCB/UI rework**, **tone/brand-template drift**, and **strict production firmware boundaries**.

---

### 1. Standout Inbox, Calendar & Personal Productivity Setups
* **07:20 Draft-Only Inbox Assistant — Tumisang Kalagobe ("Ampere" / "Amp"):**
  * Runs every weekday at **07:20** to label inbox threads, flag quiet partner/deal threads, draft replies, and deliver a one-page priority brief—leaving Tumisang ~15 minutes to review and send (strictly draft-only, human-in-the-loop). He packaged this into a reusable Cowork starter-kit prompt.
  * Also built a Cowork **"Claude for academics"** OneDrive system (using a voice-profile doc and trackers) and an **MDU prospecting engine** in Claude Code that compresses 10–20 minutes/lead of manual research into batch prequalification, ICP scoring, and decision-maker matching.
* **"Plan My Day" & Cross-Tool PM Assistant — Taya Powers:**
  * Connected Claude Code to **Gmail, Google Calendar, Drive, Granola, Asana, Figma, Zoho Desk**, and a **read-only backend follower database** (saving ~4 hours on a single day).
  * Uses a `"plan my day"` prompt to structure **1 priority, 2–3 focus blocks, meeting buffers, and a concrete first step**, plus automated task capture, Madikwe resident app usage lookups, and a **12-month churn report** categorizing structural vs. optional cancellations.
* **Asana-Anchored Context — Graeme Longman:**
  * Uses Claude Code all day with **Asana, Google Drive, and Google Calendar** connectors; routes ad hoc tasks to a private Asana board and pastes Asana task links straight into sessions so Claude pulls full task and linked-doc context immediately.
* **Obsidian "Second Brain" — Kenau Struwig & Aadil Khoodoruth:**
  * **Kenau** runs scheduled Claude skills and MCPs to ingest notes and meeting transcripts into a backlinked Obsidian knowledge base and automate bulk admin.
  * **Aadil** logs multi-agent work in Obsidian so parallel sessions retain historical context.

---

### 2. Engineering, Hardware & Data Highlights
* **Claude Code & VS Code Dominance:** In **Steven Cooper**'s July 30 survey, **CLI / Claude Code** led decisively (13+ votes vs. 6 for Claude App UI). **Arno Scholtz**, **Caleb Smit**, **Aadil Khoodoruth**, and **Matthew Coulson** favor the **VS Code extension** over raw terminal CLI to avoid text-jumbling UI glitches. **Julian Banks** and **Aadil** both recommended **Herdr (`herdr.dev`)** for managing multiple agents and preserving CLI context if a terminal closes.
* **Interactive Repo Onboarding & Infra Automation — Keelan Govender & Jane Wyngaard:**
  * **Keelan** published org-scoped interactive repo onboarding guides (`ONBOARDING.md` → `claude.ai/claude-code/onboard/...`), wired **AWS S3 security reports** into infra repo remediation summaries, and used cross-repo discovery for **RDS/Redshift decommissioning**.
  * **Jane** uses Claude to navigate **~40–50 repos**, distilling research docs and converting repeatable tasks into deterministic scripts so she stops spending tokens re-running the same work.
* **Production Code Boundaries & Tech-Debt Wins:**
  * **Steven Cooper** refuses direct AI edits on production **Solarbot/Swattbot firmware** (limiting Claude to logging and review), while vibe-coding the **Solarbot Simulator** (EnergiTrack simulation) in ~2 hours.
  * **Eben Oladutemu** fixed a **User App** edit-routine reload state bug and accelerated **Ruby Solar Lane** work.
  * **Sheila Mbadi** used Fable (while included at a capped rate) to clear multi-year tech debt upgrading **WeasyPrint** (`pydyf` vs. `cairo` PDF rendering shifts) for HotBot user reports.
  * **Matthew Coulson** sped up **Inverter Digital Twin** EDA and outlier charting; **Arno Scholtz** built repeatable data queries/dashboards on `sims.plentify.io` (GORKs, Mantis, 2G sunset, meshing, refurb issues); and **Aadil** prototyped excess-solar and scheduled **EV charging** modes on the Solarbot repo.
* **Hardware & PCB Exploration — Irshaad Dodia & Craig Burden:**
  * **Irshaad** rated Claude **7/7** for navigating Plentify's hardware knowledge base—tracing wiring across boards, reading component datasheets, and suggesting alternatives—and noted simple HW designs succeeded with minimal intervention.
  * **Craig** used **Fable 5.2** in his spare time to prototype a complex **Raspberry Pi Compute Module 5 carrier board** (for monitor-mounted production/ops stations), showing strong exploratory value despite a messy first-prompt PCB that required extensive rework.

---

### 3. Brand, Visuals & Animations
* **"Make it Plentify" Brand Kit — Chris Vey & Tamsyn Lunt:** **Chris** packaged Marketing's Brand Refresh into a drop-in `Plentify-Brand-Kit.md` for Claude Projects to style internal `.docx` outputs. **Tamsyn** noted doc headers still didn't 100% match Marketing's Google Doc templates (and `.docx` → Google Doc conversion felt tedious), whereas feeding a **PDF of a preferred deck** worked far better; **Tumisang** suggested editing blank local templates via Cowork/Code for strict consistency.
* **Presentation Animations — Jon Kornik:** Tested **Opus 5.5** on presentation GIFs (`Shiftable-appliances-image-comp-2.gif` → `Load management with batteries.gif`), successfully adding batteries while preserving the original theme, colours, and background.
* **Upcoming Experiment — Emma Hobson:** Joined on November 16 to consolidate customer feedback on the **Balwin app**.

---

### 4. Key Risks, Model Notes & Friction Flagged by the Team
* **Fable 5.2 Data Retention & Token Drain:** **Keelan Govender** warned that Anthropic retains **Fable** data for **30 days** regardless of subscription tier (avoid sharing sensitive company data), and **Aadil Khoodoruth** cautioned that Fable 5.2 rapidly burned through most of his weekly tokens (noting the free weekly reset applies *only* to Fable).
* **Opus 5.5 vs. Sonnet & Claude Design:** **Aadil** praised **Opus 5.5** for deep data/log analysis with surprisingly low token usage, while **Sonnet** remains the everyday workhorse. Both **Marelieze Dreyer** and **Aadil** noted **Claude Design** burns tokens quickly and drifts from custom UI design systems unless outputs are iterated as images in Claude Chat.
* **Tone-of-Voice & UI Bugs:** **Tamsyn Lunt** flagged sycophancy and overly theatrical prose ("open mic night for slam poetry") plus a November 11 browser UI bug where Projects temporarily disappeared after an update (resolved via support/re-login; local files were intact).
* **Governance Discipline:** **Jon Kornik** enforces monthly value check-ins to retain seats, and **Tumisang** emphasized always treating AI as a draft-only assistant requiring thorough human review.

---

### Optional Next Steps (Available on Your Approval)
* **No external actions were staged or executed.** If you would like me to stage any follow-ups—such as a Google Doc digest of these workflows, a Knowledge Base brief (`KB-RES-07`) capturing team guardrails like Fable 5.2's 30-day retention warning, or a reply in the `Claude experiment` space—just let me know.

linkedDocs.content:
Across 15 threads spanning April–November 2026 in the Claude experiment Google Chat space (spaces/AAQAly3tMR0), Plentify teammates have moved well beyond basic chat into Claude Code (CLI & VS Code) workflows for wee...

Prepared by Daniel (Guildhaven)

Executive Summary

Across 15 threads spanning April–November 2026 in the Claude experiment Google Chat space (spaces/AAQAly3tMR0), Plentify teammates have moved well beyond basic chat into Claude Code (CLI & VS Code) workflows for weekday inbox triage, calendar-anchored planning, multi-repo onboarding, legacy tech-debt cleanup, and hardware/brand prototyping. Alongside clear productivity wins, the team flagged critical guardrails around Fable 5.2's 30-day data retention and heavy token burn, complex PCB/UI rework, tone/brand-template drift, and strict production firmware boundaries.

---

1. Standout Inbox, Calendar & Personal Productivity Setups

 07:20 Draft-Only Inbox Assistant — Tumisang Kalagobe ("Ampere" / "Amp"):
   Runs every weekday at 07:20 to label inbox threads, flag quiet partner/deal threads, draft replies, and deliver a one-page priority brief—leaving Tumisang ~15 minutes to review and send (strictly draft-only, human-in-the-loop). He packaged this into a reusable Cowork starter-kit prompt.
   Also built a Cowork "Claude for academics" OneDrive system (using a voice-profile doc and trackers) and an MDU prospecting engine in Claude Code that compresses 10–20 minutes/lead of manual research into batch prequalification, ICP scoring, and decision-maker matching.
 "Plan My Day" & Cross-Tool PM Assistant — Taya Powers:
   Connected Claude Code to Gmail, Google Calendar, Drive, Granola, Asana, Figma, Zoho Desk, and a read-only backend follower database (saving ~4 hours on a single day).
   Uses a "plan my day" prompt to structure 1 priority, 2–3 focus blocks, meeting buffers, and a concrete first step, plus automated task capture, Madikwe resident app usage lookups, and a 12-month churn report categorizing structural vs. optional cancellations.
 Asana-Anchored Context — Graeme Longman:
   Uses Claude Code all day with Asana, Google Drive, and Google Calendar connectors; routes ad hoc tasks to a private Asana board and pastes Asana task links straight into sessions so Claude pulls full task and linked-doc context immediately.
 Obsidian "Second Brain" — Kenau Struwig & Aadil Khoodoruth:
   Kenau runs scheduled Claude skills and MCPs to ingest notes and meeting transcripts into a backlinked Obsidian knowledge base and automate bulk admin.
   Aadil logs multi-agent work in Obsidian so parallel sessions retain historical context.

---

2. Engineering, Hardware & Data Highlights

 Claude Code & VS Code Dominance: In Steven Cooper's July 30 survey, CLI / Claude Code led decisively (13+ votes vs. 6 for Claude App UI). Arno Scholtz, Caleb Smit, Aadil Khoodoruth, and Matthew Coulson favor the VS Code extension over raw terminal CLI to avoid text-jumbling UI glitches. Julian Banks and Aadil both recommended Herdr (herdr.dev) for managing multiple agents and preserving CLI context if a terminal closes.
 Interactive Repo Onboarding & Infra Automation — Keelan Govender & Jane Wyngaard:
   Keelan published org-scoped interactive repo onboarding guides (ONBOARDING.md → claude.ai/claude-code/onboard/...), wired AWS S3 security reports into infra repo remediation summaries, and used cross-repo discovery for RDS/Redshift decommissioning.
   Jane uses Claude to navigate ~40–50 repos, distilling research docs and converting repeatable tasks into deterministic scripts so she stops spending tokens re-running the same work.
 Production Code Boundaries & Tech-Debt Wins:
   Steven Cooper refuses direct AI edits on production Solarbot/Swattbot firmware (limiting Claude to logging and review), while vibe-coding the Solarbot Simulator (EnergiTrack simulation) in ~2 hours.
   Eben Oladutemu fixed a User App edit-routine reload state bug and accelerated Ruby Solar Lane work.
   Sheila Mbadi used Fable (while included at a capped rate) to clear multi-year tech debt upgrading WeasyPrint (pydyf vs. cairo PDF rendering shifts) for HotBot user reports.
   Matthew Coulson sped up Inverter Digital Twin EDA and outlier charting; Arno Scholtz built repeatable data queries/dashboards on sims.plentify.io (GORKs, Mantis, 2G sunset, meshing, refurb issues); and Aadil prototyped excess-solar and scheduled EV charging modes on the Solarbot repo.
 Hardware & PCB Exploration — Irshaad Dodia & Craig Burden:
   Irshaad rated Claude 7/7 for navigating Plentify's hardware knowledge base—tracing wiring across boards, reading component datasheets, and suggesting alternatives—and noted simple HW designs succeeded with minimal intervention.
   Craig used Fable 5.2 in his spare time to prototype a complex Raspberry Pi Compute Module 5 carrier board (for monitor-mounted production/ops stations), showing strong exploratory value despite a messy first-prompt PCB that required extensive rework.

---

3. Brand, Visuals & Animations

 "Make it Plentify" Brand Kit — Chris Vey & Tamsyn Lunt: Chris packaged Marketing's Brand Refresh into a drop-in Plentify-Brand-Kit.md for Claude Projects to style internal .docx outputs. Tamsyn noted doc headers still didn't 100% match Marketing's Google Doc templates (and .docx → Google Doc conversion felt tedious), whereas feeding a PDF of a preferred deck worked far better; Tumisang suggested editing blank local templates via Cowork/Code for strict consistency.
 Presentation Animations — Jon Kornik: Tested Opus 5.5 on presentation GIFs (Shiftable-appliances-image-comp-2.gif → Load management with batteries.gif), successfully adding batteries while preserving the original theme, colours, and background.
 Upcoming Experiment — Emma Hobson: Joined on November 16 to consolidate customer feedback on the Balwin app.

---

4. Key Risks, Model Notes & Friction Flagged by the Team

 Fable 5.2 Data Retention & Token Drain: Keelan Govender warned that Anthropic retains Fable data for 30 days regardless of subscription tier (avoid sharing sensitive company data), and Aadil Khoodoruth cautioned that Fable 5.2 rapidly burned through most of his weekly tokens (noting the free weekly reset applies only to Fable).
 Opus 5.5 vs. Sonnet & Claude Design: Aadil praised Opus 5.5 for deep data/log analysis with surprisingly low token usage, while Sonnet remains the everyday workhorse. Both Marelieze Dreyer and Aadil noted Claude Design burns tokens quickly and drifts from custom UI design systems unless outputs are iterated as images in Claude Chat.
 Tone-of-Voice & UI Bugs: Tamsyn Lunt flagged sycophancy and overly theatrical prose ("open mic night for slam poetry") plus a November 11 browser UI bug where Projects temporarily disappeared after an update (resolved via support/re-login; local files were intact).
 Governance Discipline: Jon Kornik enforces monthly value check-ins to retain seats, and Tumisang emphasized always treating AI as a draft-only assistant requiring thorough human review.

---

Optional Next Steps (Available on Your Approval)
• No external actions were staged or executed. If you would like me to stage any follow-ups—such as a Google Doc digest of these workflows, a Knowledge Base brief (KB-RES-07) capturing team guardrails like Fable 5.2's 30-day retention warning, or a reply in the Claude experiment space—just let me know.
